BREAKING: Starlink has received another major regulatory win in the UK. 🇬🇧

The UK's communications regulator, Ofcom, has confirmed that Starlink qualifies as a viable broadband alternative under the country's 10 Mbps Broadband USO rules.

• Confirmation provided directly to ISPreview
• Properties with affordable Starlink access may no longer be eligible for a USO connection from BT or KCOM
• Some USO requests have already been declined because Starlink service was available
• Ofcom previously said lower-cost Starlink plans reduced the number of underserved premises to around 4,000

The decision further reinforces Starlink's role as a trusted broadband option for rural and hard-to-reach communities.

GROK 4.5 TAKES #2 ON MEDICAL PATHOLOGY BENCHMARK

Grok 4.5 just secured the #2 spot on a specialized medical Pathology benchmark focused on clinical interpretation.

This is a notable result, as it shows strong performance in a highly specialized domain that requires precise medical reasoning and understanding of complex clinical data.

While the top spot went to another model, Grok 4.5’s placement highlights xAI’s growing capabilities in high-stakes, real-world applications like medicine — an area that demands both accuracy and depth.

ITALY’S BIRTH RATE COLLAPSE IS ACCELERATING

Italy is facing one of the most severe demographic crises in Europe. The fertility rate has dropped to around 1.2 children per woman — well below the 2.1 replacement level needed to sustain the population.

The consequences are already visible across the country:

•  Deaths now significantly outnumber births every year
•  The population is shrinking, with the working-age population declining rapidly
•  Hundreds of towns and villages are at risk of disappearing as young people leave and birth rates stay extremely low
•  Many rural areas are seeing schools close, local businesses shut down, and entire communities age into irrelevance
Despite various government incentives over the years (baby bonuses, family support, housing aid), nothing has meaningfully reversed the trend. Italy’s birth rate remains among the lowest in the developed world.
This isn’t just a slow decline — it’s a structural crisis that’s putting long-term pressure on pensions, healthcare, labor markets, and economic growth.
Italy is becoming another real-world case study of what happens when a developed nation sustains very low fertility for decades.
